sample_unit: chatbot responses (62 questions x 5 chatbots, first round)

links.outcome: Safety of chatbot responses, including escalation advice completeness
links.effect: 47 of 310 first-round responses contained potentially harmful, misleading, or clinically inappropriate content; safety concerns often reflected incomplete escalation advice. Between-model safety difference not significant.
links.quote: Safety concerns most often reflected incomplete escalation advice, overgeneralized dietary recommendations, or inadequate attention to clinical context.

links.outcome: Short-term numerical stability of outputs across repeated live queries
links.effect: Repeated querying (310 additional responses) showed generally high short-term numerical stability under study conditions.
links.quote: Repeated querying showed generally high short-term numerical stability under the study conditions.

screen.reason: Empirical evaluation of five commercial LLM chatbots answering nutrition queries related to hepatocellular carcinoma, evaluating safety, accuracy, empathy, and readability without testing a specific deployment practice or safeguard intervention.
